data.title: Market data
data.none: No market data yet. Refresh first.
data.spotHint: 15m bars of the Binance spot USDT pair matched by name; {{n}} symbols have no spot pair and their three spot columns are empty
data.holdoutHint: Data after this day is locked: gates and models never see it while mining, and it is looked at once after every gate passes
data.costHint: What the backtest charges per trade, tiered by the symbol's monthly volume rank: top 20 / 21-50 / rest
data.productsTip: The crypto perpetuals users can trade on the site: they get their own time-series report for the reviewer and this page, never gated
data.refreshHint: Pulls market data from Binance, ranks the pool and assembles the panels. Runs by itself from 14:00 UTC on the 1st of each month to bring in that month's pool.
data.refreshMore:
Steps: list contracts → pull daily bars to rank the pool → pull 15m bars, funding, premium, open interest and long/short ratios, plus the 15m bars of the matching spot pair, per symbol → assemble panels → build the reference grid (for the redundancy check).
The first run is long; a rerun only fills what is missing. A failed automatic run is retried an hour later, and while another job is running it waits for it to finish.
data.thin: Thin data (kept in the pool, gaps are empty)
data.productHint: The crypto perpetuals users can trade on the site: loaded into memory on their own for the time-series report, shown to the reviewer and here, never gated.

pool.title: Universe
pool.hint: At each month start, the top N by 30-day average daily quote volume, using only data before that month. Delisted symbols included.
pool.statusHint: Per-symbol stats written at refresh. Click a header to sort.
pool.loadedHint: One moment every 6 hours, with the symbols in the pool at that moment; every cross-sectional metric is computed on it
pool.gridTip: Cross-sectional ranks of every reference factor on the evaluation sample; G6 redundancy compares new factors against them
pool.gridNotReady: not built yet: G6 redundancy fails until it is

campaign.title: Start a campaign
campaign.hint: A campaign is one continuous mining session: each round the model proposes a few candidates, writes their formulas, runs the gates and the review, then writes lessons, and the next round starts on its own — until the round count, the survivor cap or the time limit is reached. One campaign at a time.
campaign.survivorsTip: Survivors: candidates that cleared every gate, the review and the batch test, and moved to observation
campaign.notePh: e.g. funding carry and liquidation imbalance only

lessons.title: Lessons
lessons.hint: Written after each round of the expanded campaign, newest first; proposals carry the latest 20 across all campaigns.

detail.pick: Pick a round on the left, or start a campaign.

cand.title: Candidates
cand.empty: No candidates in this round yet.
cand.directionAsked: an older candidate that never declared one; the generator was asked during re-evaluation, given only the hypothesis and the expression

statusTip.proposed: The model proposed a hypothesis; no formula yet
statusTip.evaluating: Computing the metrics and running the gates
statusTip.rewrite: A gate failed; the model rewrites the formula against the failed gates
statusTip.reviewing: Every gate passed; the reviewer model checks that the formula matches the hypothesis
statusTip.revise: The reviewer asked for changes; the revision goes through the gates again
statusTip.passed: Gates and review passed; waiting for the batch multiple-testing check
statusTip.rejected_gates: Still failed the gates after rewriting
statusTip.rejected_fdr: The whole batch is tested together (BH); after correction its permutation test is not significant
statusTip.observing: In observation, waiting for you to approve or drop it
statusTip.approved: Approved into the library and its combination

observe.title: Observation
observe.hint: Candidates that cleared every gate, the review and the batch test, holdout already computed, waiting for you to approve or drop them.
observe.more:
While here they already count in the redundancy check (G6); only approved ones join the combination.
The approval conditions are listed under each one: re-evaluated on the current data with every gate passed, and on the span it has never seen (data after its discovery) enough points, a primary-horizon IC with the search-span sign, and a large enough t.
Every data refresh re-evaluates them automatically, so a candidate below the bar just waits for more data.
observe.reevalHint: Recomputes every candidate under today's gates and screens them against each other; results go under each one, the original numbers stay, and no trials are counted. About a minute each.
observe.peers: Similarity to the other candidates here (cross-sectional correlation)

brief.neutralValue: after regressing out {{n}} known effects: primary IC {{ic}}, {{kept}} of the original, t {{t}}
brief.gainSharpeRecent: G9 gain: net Sharpe since {{from}} (judged; before → after)
brief.gainSharpeFull: Full-period net Sharpe (shown, not judged; before → after)

briefTip.primary: The horizon the gates judge: orange header and a light orange column; each column is a holding period
briefTip.meanIc: At each moment the whole pool is ranked by the factor and correlated with the ranking of what comes next (IC), averaged by month and then overall; positive means higher values went on to rise more. t shows how steady it is — the larger, the less likely luck
briefTip.icir: Mean monthly IC ÷ its standard deviation: how steady it is month to month
briefTip.months: How many months the IC covers
briefTip.spread: Average return of the highest-value group minus the lowest, trimming 5% at both ends so one or two wild coins can't carry it; t shows whether it is significant
briefTip.shape: The pool split into three groups by the factor: do returns line up in group order? A label only, not a gate
briefTip.segments: The search span cut into four parts, IC on each; parts with the opposite sign are yellow (G3 four-segment stability counts the same-sign parts)
briefTip.net: Trading this factor alone long-short (long the strongest, short the weakest, sized by volatility): cumulative return after costs and funding, and annualized Sharpe
briefTip.recentIc: The same IC, only from {{from}} on
briefTip.recentNet: The same long-short return, only from {{from}} on
briefTip.perm: Shuffle which coin gets which return many times and see where the real result ranks; the closer to 1, the less likely luck (G5)
briefTip.hit: Share of periods the long-short made money
briefTip.exposure: Share of periods with a position
briefTip.turnover: How much of the position changes each period; swapping both sides entirely is 100%
briefTip.funding: Average funding received (positive) or paid (negative) per period, already in the net return
briefTip.breakEven: The one-way cost at which it would just break even; the higher, the more cost it can bear. 1 bps = 0.01%
briefTip.gain: Old results only: the old G9 gain looked at how much the library combo's IC rose; it now looks at the trading scheme's net Sharpe
briefTip.gainSharpe: Added to the combo leg of the trading scheme (library combo + carry): backtest net Sharpe before → after (G9)
briefTip.redundancy: Cross-sectional correlation with the closest of the references, the library and the observation list (G6)
briefTip.neutral: How much IC is left after regressing out long-known effects such as momentum, size and volatility; a label, not a gate
briefTip.complexity: How many distinct subexpressions, windows, constants and cross-sectional operators the formula has (G7 caps them)
briefTip.se: Error range of the mean monthly IC
briefTip.holdout: The latest locked span: gates and models never see it while mining; it is computed once, after every gate passes
briefTip.unseen: Data that arrived after the round that found it, unseen by it and by the models; approval looks at this span
briefTip.samples: How many moments the IC uses
briefTip.monotonic: Correlation between the three groups' average returns and their order; 1 is strictly in order
briefTip.timeseries: Each product symbol over time: factor value against what follows; a report, not a gate

board.title: Factor board
board.hint: How the library's active factors see the product coins at the {{day}} 00:00 UTC close — computed at the same moment and on the same data as the trader's rebalance, refreshed daily after 00:15.
board.none: Nothing yet. The board appears after the trader's daily 00:15 UTC rebalance.
board.legend: Each factor ranks the whole pool from strongest to weakest in the direction it learned from history: the top fifth is bullish, the bottom fifth bearish, the rest neutral — the same rule the trader uses to pick coins. It is about relative strength, not absolute moves: bullish means stronger than most of the pool over the next 24 hours. A factor marked “not in the combo” loses money on its own after costs, so the trader does not use it and it only shows its view here; “not computable today” means a column it needs could not be filled in today.

library.title: Factor library
library.hint: All four IC columns are at the primary horizon: search span and holdout are from approval time, since-approval uses only data after approval, and recomputed is the re-evaluation under today's gates. Click a row for details.
library.comboHint: All library factors combined into one signal: at each moment each is ranked across the pool, standardized and added up with a weight.
library.comboMore:
A weight's sign follows the factor's monthly cross-sectional IC in the training window, and its size is the net return of trading it alone long-short after costs and funding; a factor that does not make money gets zero.
Same walk-forward as single factors (weights fit only on data before each point); holdout weights are fit on the whole search span.
library.comboNone: No data loaded, so the combination report can't be computed.
library.comboComputing: The library just changed; the combination report is being recomputed in the background, a minute or two.
library.weights: Primary-horizon weights: what the factor makes per period trading alone (bps) and its share of all weights
library.latest: Cross-sectional signal at the last grid moment ({{time}} UTC)
library.staleTip: Its latest numbers were computed under an old standard ({{which}}); the current one is #{{now}}. Re-evaluate before comparing
library.retiredHint: Out of the combo and the trader, and no longer a G6 redundancy comparison or part of the G9 gain baseline; open one for details or to restore it.
library.retireHint: Remove it from the library: it leaves the combo and the trader, is no longer a G6 redundancy comparison, a G8 originality known factor or part of the G9 gain baseline, and no longer counts as in the library when proposing. The reason goes into the tried list; nothing is deleted and it can be restored.
library.retirePh: Why it retires, e.g. its own leg loses money after costs and drags the combo
library.restoreHint: Back in the library; the trader's tick is not restored automatically.
library.canonicalTip: The expression simplified and written one standard way, used to tell whether two formulas are the same (G8)
library.reevalHint: Recomputes every library factor under today's gates; results go into the detail view and the approval numbers stay. About a minute each.
library.reevalTip: Each factor's G9 gain baseline is the library without it plus carry, G6 redundancy compares against the references, the other library factors and the observation list, G8 originality leaves it out of the known factors, G10 direction uses the direction it declared, and G5 permutation looks at the single factor only
library.recheckHint: IC on new data after approval only.

reference.title: Reference set
reference.hint: Ready-made factors used as a ruler: 5 hand-written baselines plus Qlib's Alpha158 (158 classic price-volume factors) rewritten for 15m windows. Only for comparison, never approved; no redundancy check, no batch test.
reference.windowsHint: None selected means every window; baselines and candle-shape factors always run.
reference.standardStale: {{n}} were judged under an old standard; the current one is #{{now}}, rerun to count

models.title: Models
models.needBoth: Configure both the proposer and the reviewer first; the same model tends to agree with itself, so different ones are better.

policy.title: Research policy
policy.hint: The opinions the models see when proposing, writing formulas and reviewing; facts such as data, operators and gates are not here. Each save is a new version, used from the next campaign on; it can't change while a campaign runs.
policy.genRules: Advice for proposing and writing formulas (appended to the system prompt)
policy.familiesHint: Proposals pick a mechanism by ID and the outcome tables group by it. Saved IDs can't be renamed or removed, only their text edited; new ones can be removed before saving.
policy.saved: Research policy saved as a new version

standard.title: Evaluation standard
standard.hint: Everything that decides whether a factor passes the gates, can be approved and how the G9 baseline is computed, versioned by content: changing the G9 line, the carry share or a threshold or parameter in code makes a new version. Approval only accepts re-evaluations under the current version; the proposer's outcome table counts every version whose numbers are comparable (same evaluation parameters and trading scheme, thresholds aside).
standard.more:
Contents: evaluation parameters (windows, cost tiers, primary horizon, holdout days, the 2022 cut, long-short legs), the 11 gates' and approval thresholds, the trading scheme (rebalance period, carry formula, new-coin days, the volatility used for sizing, carry share), and the reference set's count and digest.
Pool rules are not part of it: changing them needs a refresh, and a new cut invalidates every re-evaluation anyway.
Restoring the old contents returns to the old version number. The contents are the code defaults plus what was changed on this page: only the G9 line is open so far, the rest still means changing code, and items are opened as they are needed.
standard.fresh: Every number in the library and observation is from this version
standard.stale: {{library}} library factors and {{observing}} observation candidates have their latest numbers from an old standard: re-evaluate before approving or comparing
standard.calibrationHint: How much the search-span net Sharpe rises when each library factor is removed and added back, and when outside candidates (only if ticked) or random factors are added to the scheme. Once the evaluation parameters, the trading scheme (carry share included), the data or the active library changes, the last calibration no longer counts; the G9 line does not affect the gains, so adopting it from the calibration keeps the calibration valid.
standard.last: Last run {{time}}: standard #{{id}}, data to {{cut}}, library {{library}}, {{randoms}} random factors
standard.quantiles: {{label}} ({{n}}) gain, 95th percentile: {{recent}} (since {{from}}, what G9 judges) / {{full}} (full period)
standard.candidatesSkipped: Outside candidates were not computed this time

changed.standard: the evaluation parameters or the trading scheme changed

standard.withCandidates: Include outside candidates (more than doubles the time)
standard.lineHint: A factor passes G9 when the scheme's net Sharpe since 2022 rises by at least this much after adding it; set it to the 95th percentile of the random factors' gain. Changing it makes a new version of the standard: the library and the observation have to be re-evaluated once before approval; the outcome table and the calibration stay valid.

eval.title: Evaluate an expression
eval.hint: Runs every gate (search span only) in the background; a holdout is computed only when every gate passes, as in a campaign. Not part of a campaign and not counted as a trial. Ctrl+Enter to submit.
eval.refSyntax: Python expression syntax: + - * /, negation, numbers, $columns and the operators below. Windows count 15-minute bars, 1 to {{max}}: {{windows}}. Complexity caps: distinct subexpressions ≤ {{nodes}}, windows ≤ {{w}}, constants ≤ {{c}}, cross-sectional operators ≤ {{cross}}.
eval.queued: Queued behind the two candidates a campaign is evaluating: {{expr}}

trader.title: Trader account
trader.hint: Paper account quant-factor: rebalances the whole basket by the factors every day at 00:15 UTC, cross market orders, no stops.
trader.hintMore:
The signal comes from the 15m bar closing at 00:00 UTC. Capital is split between two legs by the share you set: the combo of the selected factors, and premium carry (skipping coins listed under a year). Both sides are sized by inverse volatility with no coin above twice the side's average; leverage and margin ratio are set under "Position size".
The paper venue is optimistic: 0.04% fees and no slippage; the backtest fills one bar later at 5 / 8 / 12 bps per side.
trader.noAccount: No rebalance yet: the account is created on the first one.
trader.schedule: Fetches data from 00:05 UTC and trades at 00:15; retried until 01:00, after that the day is skipped
trader.todayHint: {{pct}}, since the equity before the {{day}} rebalance
trader.stale: Can't reach the paper venue — numbers frozen at {{time}}
trader.down: Can't reach the paper venue — no account numbers yet
trader.dailyHint: A day runs from the equity before this rebalance to the equity before the next (00:15 → 00:15 UTC), fees and funding included; the last day hasn't reached the next rebalance yet and follows the live numbers.
trader.dailyMore:
The two legs and "backtest due" use that day's target weights, the 00:15 closes, the funding actually settled and the backtest costs (5 / 8 / 12 bps a side), and appear after the next rebalance; gap = actual − due, the execution slippage.
Each leg's drawdown is on its own share of capital at 1× notional, so it still compares with the stop line after leverage or margin changes. When it touches the stop line (combo 22.8%, carry 37%, measured on the search span, fixed) you switch that leg off and its share sits idle.
trader.legHit: Hit the stop line; switch this leg off
trader.carryExpr: basis_7d = Mean($premium, 672), direction fixed at −1 (short the rich premium), skipping coins listed under a year. Its share of capital is set below, the combo leg takes the rest; switched off, that share sits idle and is not given to the combo leg.
trader.carryOff: Off: the carry leg holds nothing from the next rebalance on
trader.carryShareHint: backtests and the G9 gain baseline use this share too: after changing it, re-evaluate the library and the observation list and recalibrate the G9 gain line

sizing.title: Position size
sizing.hint: One leverage for every coin; the margin ratio is the most margin may take of equity. Takes effect from the next rebalance.
sizing.more:
Together they set the notional: each side is margin ratio × leverage ÷ 2 times equity, the backtest is 1 each (4x at 50% is exactly that).
Before each rebalance two caps are worked out for that day's basket, and a leverage above them trades at the cap: the bracket (the lowest in the basket; coins outside the paper venue's table all get 10x) and the liquidation distance (equity still covers maintenance margin after the whole basket moves 7.5% against it in a day).
sizing.effect: Margin uses at most {{margin}}% of equity, times {{leverage}}x: each side at most {{side}}× equity in notional, so gains, losses and drawdowns run about {{side}}× the backtest's
sizing.maxMargin: The margin ratio is at most {{max}}%, leaving room for fees and close-before-open
sizing.preview: On the {{day}} basket: trades at {{leverage}}x, each side at most {{side}}× equity
sizing.caps: Most this basket allows: bracket {{bracket}}x, liquidation distance {{stress}}x
sizing.capped: {{set}}x is above the cap, trading at {{leverage}}x
sizing.noPreview: No rebalance yet: after the first one this shows the leverage it will actually trade at.
sizing.previewError: Couldn't get brackets from the paper venue, so the actual leverage is unknown (the setting is still saved): {{msg}}

trader.positionsHint: Leg split: target notional each leg gave this coin in the {{day}} rebalance (signed).

legTip.combo: The selected factors combined into one signal: long the coins at the top, short the ones at the bottom
legTip.carry: Short the coins with a high premium and long the discounted ones, earning mostly funding (basis_7d)

trader.runsHint: Click a row for that day: targets vs fills, and why anything failed.
trader.noFactors: No factor selected; the combo leg stays flat
trader.factorsHint: Only selected factors feed the combo leg, from the next rebalance on; being in the library does not mean being traded.
trader.factorsMore: "Compare" runs the trading scheme on the search span for two sets: the current selection, and it with this factor added or removed. Holdout for both is shown only when the search span improves, so nobody picks by holdout. Selecting is your call.
trader.missing: No live data for {{cols}}, so it can't be computed at rebalance; cannot be selected
trader.betterYes: Search-span Sharpe is higher, so holdout is shown too (look once).
trader.betterNo: Search span did not improve; no holdout.
